problem: VLN datasets only offer global instruction-trajectory matching; fine-grained sub-instruction/sub-trajectory and entity-landmark alignment annotations are scarce, small and expensive (human-annotated) or imprecise (heuristic), and no dataset offers both levels.
motivation: Action decisions require grounding entities in nearby views and tracking which sub-instruction is being executed, but agents only get coarse supervision. Automatically generating large-scale data with precise dual-level alignment using foundation models (GLIP, OFA, CLIP) can supply this supervision without manual annotation.
key_idea: Chunk sampled trajectories into sub-trajectories, detect landmarks with GLIP, build template-based crafted instructions, rewrite them into R2R-style sub-instructions with an OFA-based panorama-aware speaker, select the matching entity via CLIP, then concatenate to a full instruction with sub-pair and entity-landmark annotations (FCA-R2R).
insight: Augmented data with fine-grained alignment helps all agents, with larger gains for non-pretrained LSTM agents (SF +10 SR on val-unseen) than pretrained ones (HAMT +1.5 SR). Speaker ablations show panoramic input plus a panorama encoder and fine-tuning the decoder are key to instruction quality (CIDEr 11.79 vs 4.56 without pano on val unseen), and SimCTG contrastive decoding reduces repetition over greedy.
method: Trajectory chunking: sample 5-7 step trajectories in MP3D and split by turning angle (straight/right/left/backward); consecutive straight steps form one sub-trajectory, each turn its own.

Landmark detection: GLIP with a per-environment landmark category library (from GEL-R2R), restricted to a 180° sector along the movement direction, picks the highest-confidence object/scene as landmark per sub-trajectory.
Crafted instruction construction: 108 templates (12 horizontal turn types x 3 vertical x 3 landmark-relative positions) filled with detected landmarks.

R2R-like generation (OFA-Speaker): OFA-base plus panorama encoder (spatial and temporal Transformer layers over CLIP-ViT view features); input is prompt + crafted instruction + panoramas; trained on R2R with GEL-R2R-derived crafted instructions in two phases (frozen OFA, then full fine-tune); SimCTG loss and contrastive search decoding.
Entity selection: NLTK extracts candidate entities from the generated sub-instruction; CLIP cosine similarity to the landmark crop picks the entity, forming an entity-landmark pair.

Sub-pair integration: concatenate sub-instructions into a full instruction and shift entity marker positions, yielding FCA-R2R (178,270 trajectories, 534,810 instructions, 2.52M sub-pairs, 5.24M entity-landmark pairs).

setting.backbone: OFA-base speaker (fine-tuned) with GLIP and CLIP (frozen) for data generation; followers SF, EnvDrop, RecBERT, HAMT, Babywalk, AFAC, GELA (trained)
setting.training_data: Speaker trained on R2R train with GEL-R2R-based crafted instructions; followers trained/pretrained with the generated FCA-R2R (534,810 instructions over 178,270 trajectories) replacing the original augmentation data, plus R2R
setting.action_space: Discrete navigable viewpoints on the nav-graph plus STOP
setting.privileged: none (data generation uses the connectivity graph and environment poses in training environments)

numbers.backbone: GELA (adaptive pre-training with FCA-R2R entity-landmark pairs)

numbers.extra: FCA-R2R augmentation data; row labelled 'val test' in the paper

numbers_note: Speaker language-quality results (BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE/CIDEr) are in ablation tables and not listed as navigation numbers. Additional variants (SF, EnvDrop, Babywalk +FCA-R2R) are in Tables 2-3.
results: Replacing standard augmentation with FCA-R2R improves SF, EnvDrop, RecBERT and HAMT on val-unseen (e.g., SF SR 35.0→45.0; HAMT SPL 60.9→61.5). With GELA, it reaches SR 71.1/68.3 and SPL 65.5/63.3 on val-unseen/test-unseen, slightly above GELA trained on human-annotated GEL-R2R (SPL 65.0/62.1).
limitations: Gains for strong pretrained agents are small (SR +0.0 to +1.5 on val-unseen for GELA/HAMT) and some metrics degrade (SF val-seen SR, AFAC val-seen NE).
Data quality depends on GLIP detection and the speaker; alignment accuracy of generated annotations is not directly evaluated against human labels.
Only evaluated on R2R-style discrete Matterport3D navigation, with no real-world or continuous-environment tests.
